title: The Silent Loop Line
notes: Recurring detective-cast (Conan, Kogoro, Ran, Inspector Megure, Officer Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: actions are direct typed edges. Transcript spells the victim's given name 'Kiyoumi' in dialogue; kept as 'Kiyomi Hashimoto' per the v1 scaffold's romanization, noted as an alias. Two red herrings survive from the group interrogation scene: Kurata's rejected romantic pursuit of the victim, and Kawai's accusation that the victim plagiarized her ad designs -- both raised on-screen as motives before being set aside for lack of opportunity. case_type: murder.

attrs.note: repeatedly gave the victim gifts and pursued her romantically; she turned him down each time
once accused the victim of plagiarizing her ad designs
youngest of the four coworkers; deliberately made a work mistake the day before to force everyone into Sunday overtime together, setting up the alibi dinner

attrs.died_of: poisoned pin (South American blow-dart poison) hidden under a headphone sponge cover, pierced her ear when she put the headphones on
attrs.died_where: alone in the second train car of the Kanjo loop line; found when the train looped back to where she boarded

locations.name: Kanjo (JR Yamanote) loop line train, second car
Restaurant used for the group's alibi dinner

attrs.mechanism: a pin coated in fast-acting South American blow-dart poison, hidden under the headphone's foam ear cover; pierced the wearer's ear on contact
attrs.acquired: the culprit said she obtained the poison a few days earlier on an overseas trip
attrs.staging_flaw: one earpiece was snapped when the culprit yanked the headphones off the body, which had stiffened with rigor mortis and was pinned between the victim's shoulder and the train wall

attrs.note: lent to the victim in place of her own, broken player, with the poisoned headphones already attached

objects.name: MD disc inside the loaned player, with a cut/obscured label

attrs.hidden_message: 'Thank you, Yukiko. -- Kiyomi', handwritten in pink ballpoint pen, partly cut off by the label trim
attrs.significance: the disc was labeled with that day's date, contradicting Mori's claim that she had not lent Kiyomi anything that day

attrs.note: broken earlier that day when Mori dropped it, creating the pretext to lend her the rigged replacement
used to pull the poisoned pin out of the body without leaving fingerprints; the pin itself was never recovered
ink matched the handwriting on the MD disc's hidden thank-you message

clues.desc: Label-ink comparative clue: pink ink visible along the trimmed edge of the MD disc's label matches the pink ballpoint pen found in the victim's purse, revealing a hidden handwritten message ('Thank you, Yukiko') that the disc's outward label was cut to hide.

Retrieval-struggle clue: an unusual pressure mark/imprint from the headphone jack was left on the victim's arm, her shirt collar had been jerked upward, and one headphone earpiece was snapped -- consistent with someone forcibly and hurriedly pulling the headphones off a rigor-mortis-stiffened body rather than the victim removing them herself.

edges.detail: dropped and broke Kiyomi's MD player, giving herself a pretext to lend a replacement
lent her own MD player with the pre-poisoned headphones attached, in place of the broken one

edges.method: poisoned pin hidden in the headphone sponge cover pierced her ear when she put them on

edges.detail: used the group alibi dinner as cover; briefly excused herself claiming she wanted to buy juice
boarded the second car, having timed the loop line's ~70-minute circuit to know the body would be back at the boarding station
pulled the poisoned headphones off the rigor-mortis-stiffened body, snapping an earpiece and jerking the collar
used the handkerchief to remove and dispose of the poison pin without leaving fingerprints

edges.motive_type: revenge (the victim had taken her boyfriend; the murder was deliberately timed to his birthday)
romantic_rejection (red herring; had pursued her with gifts and been repeatedly turned down)
professional_grievance (red herring; accused the victim of plagiarizing her ad designs)
